subject: Kickoff: Evaluation MAP + Benchmarks — Aurora Health POC
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@aurorahealth.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Evaluation MAP + Benchmarks — Aurora Health POC

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off a lightweight Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the Aurora Health POC so we have clear owners, success criteria, and a short timeline to close. I’ve sketched a first-pass plan below — please review and confirm owners or edits.

High-level POC objectives (proposed):
- Validate clinical note summarization quality on 3 representative departments (ED, Cardiology, Oncology)
- Verify 95th-percentile latency under 300ms for 512-token requests in staging
- Measure cost-per-1k-tokens and validate caching/quantization impact
- Confirm security / data handling meets Aurora procurement/information security needs

Proposed timeline: 4–6 weeks from kickoff (I left a short buffer but happy to tighten).
Week 0: Kickoff + MAP sign-off
Week 1: Dataset ingestion + baseline runs
Week 2: Focused prompt tuning and quality evals
Week 3: Latency/cost benchmarking and canary deployment in staging
Week 4: Final report + review (deliverable: bench report + redwood eval template)

Proposed owners (please confirm):
- Redwood PM / AE: Jasmine Liu — overall MAP owner, meeting cadence, deliverables
- SE / Benchmarks: Marcus Lin — latency, throughput, cost experiments
- Quality / Eval design: Rishi Malhotra — prompt sets, automated evals, human labels
- Customer success / rollout: Marissa Cole — staging rollout & canary coordination

Success criteria (examples, editable):
- Avg BLEU/ROUGE improvements vs baseline prompt >= 15% on target datasets
- Human acceptability >= 85% on clinical summary samples
- 95th perc. token latency < 300ms in staging under simulated load
- No open unresolved security items beyond low severity by final delivery

Attachments: redwood-eval-template-v2.docx (baseline bench template + eval rubric)
HubSpot MAP draft: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ah-2027-042

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the Aurora stakeholders who will own approvals, security sign-off, and procurement?
2) Confirm you’re comfortable with a 4-week compressed timeline, or we can extend to 6 weeks if necessary.
3) Suggest a 30-minute alignment call Monday 4/5 at 09:00 PT or Tuesday 4/6 at 11:00 PT — which works?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out together.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
-- attachment: redwood-eval-template-v2.docx (docx; 75 KB)
From: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 14:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evaluation MAP + Benchmarks — Aurora Health POC

Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear plan and the template. A couple quick notes from our side:
- We’re aiming to keep the POC to 4 weeks if possible; the clinical governance board wants a faster read. If we can compress Weeks 1–3 into a tighter schedule that’d be ideal.
- Security / compliance is critical: Tom (cc’d) will lead technical security sign-off (SOC2, data retention, and audit logging). Can you add a security checklist item and a contact for your security/ops team?
- Procurement: I’ve looped in Procurement for contract/PO cadence. Emily Park will be our procurement lead (she’ll follow up separately).

We can do a quick kickoff call Monday 4/5 at 09:00 PT — that works for me.

I attached a short doc with Aurora’s basic POC requirements.

—Sarah
Sarah Kline
Head of Clinical AI | Aurora Health
-- attachment: aurora-poc-requirements.pdf (pdf; 120 KB)

Jasmine / team —

Helpful start, Sarah — thanks for the note. Quick sequencing and owners for the benchmark side (internal):

Bench plan (Marcus lead):
- Day 0–2: Ingest sample datasets (ED, Cardiology, Oncology) into isolated staging buckets; verify PII handling and retention settings. (owner: Marcus)
- Day 3–6: Run baseline model passes (current open model) and record token counts/latency under 1, 5, and 10 qps simulated load. (owner: Marcus)
- Day 7–10: Run prompt variants and measure quality delta with automated evals (owner: Rishi)
- Day 11–15: Quantization + cache experiments to estimate cost curve (owner: Marcus)
- Day 16–20: Compile bench report and a short Canaries playbook for Marissa to roll into staging (owner: Marissa)

Metrics we’ll deliver:
- 95th percentile latency (ms) for 256/512 token requests at nominal load
- Cost per 1k tokens across baseline vs quantized profiles
- Automated eval scores + human acceptability samples (Rishi to define sampling rate)
- A short risk register for anything blocking security sign-off (we’ll need Tom’s inputs on acceptable audit/logging levels)

Can Rishi confirm the eval rubric thresholds (I’d propose human acceptability >= 85% and automated score delta >= 12%)? Also Jasmine, I’ll prepare a short runbook for ingest and test data handling for Tom’s review.

- Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
